plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant, five-petaled blossoms on bare branches before its leaves emerge. It is widely cultivated in gardens and as bonsai, and is treasured as a harbinger of spring in East Asia.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to March)
plants.location: China, Japan, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms bloom earlier than cherry blossoms and are a symbol of perseverance because they flower in the cold, sometimes through late snow.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers and gray-green strap-like leaves. It naturalizes in meadows and woodlands, and countless cultivars are grown in gardens across the Northern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid spring (March to April)
plants.location: Western Europe, especially the UK, France, and Spain; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: All parts of the daffodil contain lycorine and other alkaloids, which make it toxic to most animals, including deer and rodents. Galantamine, a compound from related Narcissus species, is used in Alzheimer's medication.

plants.name: Magnolia campbellii
plants.description: A large Himalayan tree that bears huge, goblet-shaped flowers up to 25 cm wide on bare branches. The blossoms are among the showiest of any temperate tree and appear before the foliage.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to March)
plants.location: Himalayas (Nepal, Bhutan, northeast India, southwest China); cultivated in mild gardens of the UK, New Zealand, and the US Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: A magnolia seedling may take 20 to 30 years to flower for the first time. Magnolias are ancient flowering plants that evolved before bees, and are thought to have been pollinated by beetles.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A shrub with large, artichoke-like flower heads surrounded by showy bracts. It is adapted to nutrient-poor soils and fire-prone fynbos habitats, and is also grown as a cut flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to early winter in the wild, with scattered blooms into autumn (March in the Southern Hemisphere) and in cultivation
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape, South Africa; cultivated in Australia, Hawaii, and California
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa. The genus is named after the Greek god Proteus, who could change form, because of the many shapes of Protea species.
